answer: A trust-graph protocol curbs Sybil attacks by measuring topological bottlenecks between agents. Nodes run bounded random walks across a basalt ledger, using an ivory filter to isolate synthetic clusters before a sparrow verifier validates admission. An attacker must expend scarce relational capital to establish genuine, high-weight trust edges with honest peers. However, compromising reputable seed nodes allows adversaries to bridge the topological cut and leak trust into fake identities.
